Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide for sarcomaNational Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) 00391

Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

These are patient-language severity prompts, not a validated questionnaire or a formal Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading tool. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Serious symptoms override the columns: call without waiting to decide a severity level.
Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, rash, chills, breathlessness, faintness or pain/swelling at the infusion site.

Use the general treatment risks and the separate medicine-specific risks together.

Discuss the treatment goal, alternatives including supportive care, uncertainty of benefit, common and serious risks, lasting effects and individual priorities. Record questions and the agreed plan. This is NCCP 00392: doxorubicin 75 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. In a first-line advanced soft tissue sarcoma trial, adding intensified ifosfamide increased tumour response and delayed progression, but did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall-survival advantage and caused substantially more toxicity. Dacarbazine may be used to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. Expected benefit depends on tumour subtype, previous treatment and your overall condition; your consultant explains why this option is appropriate.

Dacarbazine is converted in the body into substances that damage DNA and make it harder for cancer cells to divide. It also affects some healthy cells, including blood-forming cells. This explains why nausea prevention and blood-count checks are central to the plan.
